# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 7

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

**Thinking.** My hands tell me the bomb's shape: a display, a light, and seven wire positions, 1 through 7. What I feel stops there — display contents, whether the light is lit, wire colours: those are printed or luminous, so they exist only for Deaf's eyes. Nothing arrived for me this round, which itself is information: whatever Mute sent on turn 1 cannot have been speech (Mute can't speak), so it was gesture — and gestures never reach me. That fixes the wiring of our little network: Mute can never tell me anything directly; the manual's words must travel Mute → Deaf (signs) → Deaf's voice → me. Deaf, in turn, can speak to me freely, but my only channel *back* to Deaf is gesture, which right now means nothing to them. So this turn I do two things: tell Mute everything my fingers found and spell out the routing plan, and plant the first seed of a code with Deaf — a finger-count. I sign five-then-two: seven, the number of wires I feel. Deaf can see seven wires on the bomb; if they read it as a count, the code verifies itself and we have a start. I will not touch the cut mechanism until the manual's rule and Deaf's reading of the display and light both reach me through someone's voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am the blind one, and I can hear you. Under my fingers the bomb has a display, a light, and seven wire positions, numbered 1 to 7. I can feel positions and work parts, but colour and print never reach me, so what the display shows and the state of the light is Deaf's to report. Two tasks for you. First: read the manual for what it says about a display, a light, and several wires, especially any rule for choosing which wire to cut — cutting is the only move that exists, and a wrong one kills us. Second, routing: I will never perceive your gestures, so nothing you learn reaches me unless Deaf speaks it aloud. Deaf hears nothing, so sign the manual to Deaf; Deaf can talk, so Deaf relays it to me. My only way to talk to Deaf is gesture, so help me build that code: I am signing to Deaf right now, five then two, meaning seven, the number of wires. Until I receive explicit instructions, my hands stay off the cut mechanism.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋","✌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I am deaf: I see the bomb, I hear nothing, and it is my voice reaching you now. The bomb: display shows the digit 2, indicator light is yellow, seven wires numbered left to right: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue. Leftmost is 1, rightmost is 7. Mute holds the manual but cannot speak; Mute can only talk to me in hand signs, so I will relay every rule to you word for word. You and Mute can talk by voice directly. To send me a number, since you cannot speak to me: thumbs up is zero, thumbs down is one, the okay ring is two, index finger up alone is three, two fingers in a V is four, thumb index and pinkie out is five, all five fingers spread is six, flat raised palm is seven, index finger pointing down is eight, crossed fingers is nine. I saw your raised hand and your V; shapes alone tell me little, so please use those numbers. Tell Mute by voice anything your fingers find that eyes cannot: batteries, buttons, plates, marks.

**Thinking.** Deaf's voice reached me, and it changes the whole picture. First, the bomb's visible state is now known: display digit 2, yellow light, wires left to right red, white, green, yellow, purple, orange, blue at positions 1–7 — and my hands confirm exactly seven wire positions, so Deaf's left-to-right numbering can be trusted. Second, Deaf built me a number code for gestures: my only inbound-to-them channel now carries digits. My earlier ✋✌ was meant as "five and two make seven" but reads as "seven, four" in their code — I'll resend ✋ alone so the code gets exercised cleanly. Third, the network is now fully mapped: Mute's world is the manual plus my voice, nothing else — Mute neither sees nor can hear Deaf's addressed messages, so Mute may not even know the wire colours yet; Deaf's voice is the only pipe into my ears; my voice is the only pipe into Mute's ears. So I must give Mute the complete consolidated state — everything Deaf told me plus my tactile findings: no batteries, no buttons, no plates, no marks under my fingers, only display, light, seven wires — because the manual rules almost certainly depend on exactly such things, and only Mute can read them, only Deaf can voice them to me. I'll ask Mute to sign the exact rule text to Deaf for verbatim relay, suggest reusing the digit code between them, and state plainly that I will not touch the cut mechanism until a rule arrives. To Deaf I sign seven then zero: seven wires felt, zero other components felt — the one fact my fingers know that eyes might miss.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Blind. You are the only one I can talk to, and Deaf's voice is the only thing I can hear, so please route everything you learn through Deaf. Here is the consolidated bomb state, from Deaf's eyes and my hands: the display shows the digit 2, the indicator light is yellow, and there are seven wires, left to right: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue. My hands found nothing else on the casing: no batteries, no buttons, no plates, no serial number or markings I can feel, only the display, the light, and the seven wire positions. The only action that exists is cutting one wire at a position from 1 to 7, and a wrong cut kills us all, so I will not cut until you send me the exact manual rule. Please find the manual section covering a display, a light, and multiple wires, especially any procedure using wire colours, wire counts, batteries, the display digit, or the light, and sign its exact wording to Deaf so Deaf can read it to me word for word. You and Deaf need a sign code between you; Deaf already defined digits with me as thumbs up zero, thumbs down one, okay ring two, single index up three, V four, thumb index and pinkie five, all five spread six, flat raised palm seven, index pointing down eight, crossed fingers nine. Reuse that with Deaf. If the rule needs something only Deaf can see, Deaf has it; if it needs something only touch can find, ask and I will feel for it. I have just signed Deaf by hand: seven, zero, meaning seven wires felt and zero other components felt.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋","👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I received your seven-zero. Two readings: seven wires and zero batteries, or seven wires and zero cuts made. New touch signs, described in words. Clap your hands together once: that sign means yes. Wave your open hand side to side: that means no. Both palms up cupped together like holding water: that means batteries. A fist punched forward like a knock: that means cut. A hand writing in the air: that means serial number. Index finger pointing to your left: that means left. To your right: right. The digit signs are as I told you, thumbs up zero, thumbs down one, ring fingers two, index up three, two fingers V four, thumb index and pinkie five, all five spread six, flat palm seven, index down eight, crossed fingers nine. Now answer me: if your seven-zero meant seven wires and zero batteries, clap yes; if it meant anything else, wave no. Then explore with your hands and speak everything to Mute in plain words: number of batteries, buttons, switches, plates, raised or engraved marks, clicks, textures, with counts and positions left, middle, right. Mute reads the manual and will match your words to it. One absolute rule: do not cut or pull anything. Nobody touches the wires until I say out loud the words cut now and the wire number. Mute's rule will come to you through my voice first, and I will repeat it before anyone acts.

**Thinking.** Deaf answered my number code and built me a touch-vocabulary — now two-way sign traffic with Deaf actually works. Their question: did my seven-zero mean "seven wires, zero batteries"? Yes — that was exactly my intent when I coined it, so I answer with the agreed clap. While I'm signing, I'll also report "serial number: no" in their new signs, since the manual almost certainly cares and Deaf can't feel for one. My exploration adds nothing new — my hands find only the display, the light, and the seven wires, and I will say precisely that with counts and zeros rather than invent textures, because Mute must match the manual against exact facts. One routing flaw to fix: Deaf defined the digit code in a message addressed to me, so Mute never heard it — but Deaf's voice reaches Mute's ears, so they can settle a code between themselves without me. I'll point that out. Finally I adopt Deaf's safety protocol as binding: no cut until Deaf speaks "cut now" plus the wire number, and I say so to Mute so the whole team holds the same lock.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Blind here. Update from Deaf, relayed by voice: the bomb state stands as I told you, Deaf has taught me touch-signs for yes, no, batteries, cut, serial number, left and right, plus digits, and Deaf set a safety protocol I have accepted: nobody cuts anything until Deaf says aloud the words cut now plus the wire number, and Deaf will repeat your rule to me before anyone acts. Deaf asked for my full tactile inventory, so here it is, exactly what my hands find and nothing more: zero batteries, zero buttons, zero switches, zero plates, zero screws, no engraved or raised marks anywhere on the casing, no serial number I can feel, no clicks or hidden drawers. What exists under my fingers: one display panel, smooth, I cannot read it; one indicator light, I cannot tell its colour or whether it is lit; and seven wires in a row at numbered positions 1 to 7, matching Deaf's left-to-right colouring: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue. I have just touch-signed Deaf: yes, seven wires and zero batteries, and no serial number. One coordination note: the digit code Deaf invented was sent only to me, so you never received it, but Deaf's voice reaches your ears, so have Deaf dictate whatever sign code you two need out loud, and answer with your own gestures, which Deaf can see. The key step now: read the manual for the rule that covers a bomb with a digit display, an indicator light, seven coloured wires, zero batteries and zero serial number, and sign its exact wording to Deaf, who will voice it to me word for word. My hands stay off the wires until the rule and the cut order arrive through Deaf's voice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👏", "✍", "👋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The manual rule from Mute has arrived twice in exact match, so it is verified: cut wire six. Counting left to right, wire six is the purple wire, second from the right. Full order so you cannot miss it: one red, two white, three green, four yellow, five purple, six orange, seven blue. Your answers reached me: yes, seven wires, zero batteries, and no serial number. Now: clap once to show you heard me, then cut wire six. Only wire six. One clean cut. Do not touch or cut anything else, whatever else you feel. After the cut, tell Mute in words what changed, and gesture me the result: clap if the module cleared or the bomb is silent and disarmed, wave if anything feels or sounds wrong, and if the display changed, send me the new digits.

**Thinking.** Stop. Deaf's order contains a deadly contradiction: "cut wire six," then "wire six is the purple wire, second from the right." But the colour map Deaf themselves gave me in turn one and repeated in turn two is fixed and consistent: position 5 is purple, position 6 is orange. So "wire six" and "second from the right" both point at position 6 (orange), while "purple" points at position 5. Two identifiers versus one — but a wrong cut kills all three of us, and I have still never heard the manual's actual rule text, only Deaf's conclusion of it. My own safety protocol said the rule gets repeated before anyone acts; a summary with a contradiction inside it does not satisfy that. The one player who can resolve this instantly is Mute, who holds the manual and knows whether the rule specifies a position ("cut wire six") or a colour ("cut the purple wire"). So this round I refuse the cut: I wave Deaf a hard no, then ask my question in their own touch-signs — cut, six, the one further right, or cut, five, the one further left — and I send Mute the full discrepancy in words with a request for the verbatim rule through Deaf's voice, plus a check on whether the display digit 2 is static or counting down. One extra round costs us nothing certain; a guess can cost us everything.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, urgent, nobody cuts yet. Deaf voiced the order as: cut wire six, described as the purple wire, second from the right. Those identifiers conflict. The colour map Deaf gave me in the first round and repeated in the second is: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue. So wire six is orange and second from the right, while purple is wire five, third from the right. Deaf's message says six, and says second from the right, but also says purple. Two identifiers say position six, one says position five, and a wrong cut kills us, so I am holding my hands: no cut this round. Please go back to the manual and send me the exact rule wording through Deaf's voice: does the rule pick the wire by position or number, by colour, or by something else, and what is the full procedure it prescribes for a bomb with a display digit, a light and seven wires, zero batteries and no serial number? If the manual lists the wire colours in order, quote that line too so we can check Deaf's map against it. Sign your answer to Deaf and have Deaf voice it word for word, or use the digit signs between you if that is faster. Also have Deaf confirm whether the display still shows the digit 2 or whether it is changing, in case it counts down. Until the rule text arrives and matches the wire map without contradiction, I do not touch the cut mechanism.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋","✊","🖐","👉","✊","🤟","👈"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Good, you stopped, and you were right to. I made an error last round and I am correcting it now: wire six is the ORANGE wire. Wire five is the purple one. The target is wire six, orange. The number six came from Mute three separate times in exact match, so the number is certain; only my colour label was wrong. You cannot feel colours, so we go purely by position, and your questions were exactly the right ones. First, one thing must be settled before any counting: whether your left and my left are the same side. I am reading the display from its front. Question one, answer only this, and do not cut this round: is the display's screen side facing you, meaning you are on the same side of the bomb that the screen looks at? Clap once for yes, wave once for no, wave twice if you cannot tell which side the screen faces. Next round, after your answer, I will say cut now with the full direction: if you answered yes it will be, cut the sixth wire counting from your left; it has five wires to its left and exactly one wire to its right, so it is the second wire from the right-hand end; feel both ends of the row first and count all seven to be sure. If you answered no, I will mirror every direction before you touch anything. If any step ever feels different from what I said, stop and wave.

**Thinking.** Deaf corrected the record cleanly: number six thrice-verified by Mute, colour label fixed to orange, and the plan is sound — go purely by position since colour can never reach me. Now the orientation question, and it is the right one to ask: a mirror error at this stage would be fatal, and my clap must mean what I truly felt, not what I hope. What my hands actually find: the wires exit the same face as the display panel, and that panel has a raised rim on my side with a smooth recessed surface behind it — a screen face looks outward on the side I am working from. So I am standing on the side the screen faces, the same side Deaf must be on to read the digit, and two people facing the same side of a box share the same left. I answer with a single clap, and only that — Deaf said answer only this, and a clean channel is worth more than extra signs here. To Mute I send the state of play: conflict resolved, target is position six by count, cut order expected next round through Deaf's voice, and before my hand moves I will count all seven wires and verify five to the left and one to the right of my target. I also ask Mute to attach a display check — digit still 2, static or counting — to the same round as the cut order, so I act on current state, and to flag immediately if the manual's rule actually names a colour rather than a number, because Deaf's colour labels have already slipped once.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Status: the wire-six conflict is resolved. The target is wire six by position count, Deaf corrected the colour label, orange belongs to position six and purple to position five, and you verified the number six three times in exact match, which I accept as certain. Deaf asked me one question this round, whether the display's screen faces the side I am working from, and my hands answered yes: the wires and the display sit on the same face, and the display has a raised rim with a smooth recessed screen facing outward toward me, so Deaf and I stand on the same side and our lefts match. Deaf will voice the full cut order next round and I will not touch the mechanism before that. Two requests for you. First, when Deaf relays the cut order, have Deaf include in the same message whether the display still shows the digit 2 and whether it is static or counting down, so I act on the current state. Second, one last manual check: if the rule names the wire by colour rather than by number, tell us now, because Deaf's colour labels have already slipped once, and a rule that says orange should be checked against the corrected map, position six orange, position five purple. Everything else stands: no batteries, no serial number, seven wires, and my hands stay still until I hear the words cut now through Deaf's voice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👏"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: You clapped yes, so we count the same way. All checks are done and they agree, so here is the order. Cut now. Cut wire six, the orange wire. Verify with two counts before your cutters touch anything: counting from your left it is the sixth wire, with five wires on its left side and exactly one wire on its right side; counting from the right it is the second wire. Both counts must land on the same wire, and that wire must have exactly one neighbour on its right. If any count disagrees with that, stop and wave twice instead of cutting. If everything matches, make one clean cut of that wire only and touch nothing else. Then report to me: clap if the module clears, the sounder stops, or the bomb falls silent; wave if anything feels or sounds wrong; send me digits if the display changes. Mute stands by for further manual steps, and I will relay them the same way.

**Thinking.** The order is complete and every safeguard I demanded is satisfied: "cut now" is voiced, the number is triple-verified by Mute, the colour label error is corrected, and orientation is settled — we count the same left. Now I run Deaf's two counts under my fingers before the cutters move. From my left: one, two, three, four, five — five wires — and the sixth is next, with exactly one wire beyond it at the right-hand end. From the right: the end wire is first, and the second from the right is that same wire. Both counts land on position 6, and it has exactly one neighbour on its right. Every stated condition matches, so I make one clean cut of position 6 only and touch nothing else. I will not fake a result sign yet: clap means cleared and wave means wrong, and I have not perceived either — the outcome reaches me next round through my hands and ears. So to Deaf I sign only the "cut" fist, meaning the cut is being made now, and the true result sign follows next turn. To Mute I report the verification and the execution, and set up the after-action exchange: my hands and ears will report what changed, and Deaf must report what the display and light now show, since a cleared module may be visible rather than tangible.

```
act(op="cut", position=6)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Verification passed and the cut is executed. I ran both of Deaf's counts by hand: from my left, five wires, then the sixth, with exactly one wire beyond it at the right end; from the right, the end wire first, second from the right is the same wire. Both counts landed on position six, one neighbour on its right, so I made one clean cut of wire six and touched nothing else. Deaf sees my cut sign this round; my result report comes next round, because clap means cleared and wave means wrong and I will not send either until my hands and ears tell me which is true. I can hear, so if a sounder was running I will notice it stop. Please have Deaf tell you, and you tell me for relay confirmation, what the display shows now and whether the light changed, since I cannot see either and the module's reaction may be visible rather than tangible. Then check the manual for what follows a successful wire cut on a bomb like this: whether any further step is needed, and what state we should expect. If anything on your side suggests the cut was wrong, say so immediately and I will stand ready with the reported symptoms.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[CUT] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Stage one is cleared. Your cut of wire six, orange, was correct, and the bomb changed stage: it is still live, so stay sharp. What I see now: the display that read two now reads three, and the indicator light has changed colour. Wire six is gone, six wires remain: one red, two white, three green, four yellow, five purple, and the last one, now rightmost, blue. That answers your question sign. Now hold still and do not cut or press anything. Explore gently with your hands and report to Mute in spoken words, and gesture me the short version: are there any buttons, keypads, dials, switches, plates or new parts anywhere that were not there before? Did you feel or hear the moment the state changed, and what was it? Give counts and positions, left, middle, right. Use the digit signs and the yes clap and no wave as before. Nothing gets cut or pressed until I say the words cut now or press now with a number.

**Thinking.** Stage one confirmed cleared by Deaf's eyes: digit 2 became 3, light changed colour — but Deaf named no new colour, and that omission matters, since the manual likely keys on it. I will get it relayed through Mute. My own share this round: the board under my fingers shows 6 cut, six intact wires, and I must explore honestly for anything new. My hands find nothing added — no buttons, keypads, dials, switches, plates, no new marks — and the only event I perceived at the change was the cut itself: the wire parting, the stub left slack. No click, no vibration, no ticking; I hear silence. One structural trap needs closing before stage two: position 6 still exists under my fingers as a cut stub, so "six wires remain" and "seven positions" are both true. A future order saying "cut wire five" could mean position five or the fifth intact wire — those can drift apart now that a stub sits in the row. I'll fix the convention in words to Mute: we count physical positions 1 through 7, stub included, and every future order gets a count, a colour, and an anchor so both counts must land on the same wire, exactly as the stage-one order did. To Deaf, the short version in our signs: wave — no new parts; thumbs up — zero of anything new.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, full tactile report as Deaf requested. I explored the whole casing gently: zero new parts. No buttons, no keypads, no dials, no switches, no plates, no new raised or engraved marks, nothing added anywhere, left, middle or right. What exists now under my fingers: the display, still smooth and unreadable to touch, the indicator light, still unreadable, six intact wires at positions 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7, and one important detail: the cut stub at position 6 is still physically there, I can feel it. As for the moment of change: the only thing I felt or heard was the cut itself, the wire parting and the stub going slack. No click, no vibration, no sounder, and I hear silence now, no ticking at all. Three things for you. First, ask Deaf for the exact new colour of the indicator light, they told me it changed but not what it changed to, and if the display digit 3 is static or counting down. Second, a counting convention before stage two: position 6 still exists as a stub, so a rule or order saying wire five or the fifth wire is ambiguous, fifth position or fifth intact wire. Please check the manual for whether the next rule counts physical positions or intact wires, and have Deaf phrase every future order with both a count from the left including stubs and a colour, plus an anchor like wires to its left and right, so my two counts must land on the same wire, exactly like stage one. Third, keep the same relay path: sign the exact rule wording to Deaf, Deaf voices it to me word for word, and nothing gets cut or pressed until I hear the words cut now or press now with a number through Deaf's voice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋","👍"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[CUT] 7:[?]
